proof_summary: Take \(n=p=2\): at input \(4\), the numerator and denominator products are both \(96\), so \(a(4)=1\) and hence \(\operatorname{ord}_2(a(4))=0\). On the proposed right-hand side, the \(i=0\) term is \(\lfloor 2/2\rfloor=1\), while every term for \(i\ge 1\) is zero, so the sum is \(1\), contradicting the claimed equality.
